text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leaders of Baltic countries were satisfied with the results of Madrid summit.
- The 10th international folk festival Baltica'97 began in Riga.
- Near Bikur Holim hospital in Riga police found a bomb with about 400 grams of TNT. Police said there was no evidence the bomb was aimed directly at the Jewish hospital.
- The prosecutors office may check alleged violations of the anti-corruption law by the chief of the Latvian state police, Aldis Lieljuksis.

- Interior Minister Dainis Turlais announced that five people have been dismissed an eight will be disciplined, among them three high-ranking official after the investigation of of the Talsi incident, when eight children died as a fire rescue basket plunged to the ground.
- The newspaper says Turlais is considering joining the Latvia's Way party.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Abright will meet the foreign ministers of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia on July 13 in Vilnius to discuss bilateral relations and the NATO summit.

- President Guntis Ulmanis told a press conference in Madrid that Latvia feels more secure after the Madrid meeting. The admission of Baltic states to NATO could happen within the next 5-7 years, he added.
- The press secretary of the foreign ministry said the first meeting of the Latvian-Russian intergovernmental commission will take place this autumn.
- Parekss bank and the administration of Kursk region in Russia signed an agreement on financial services and the allocation of credits worth 130 billion roubles ($25 million).
- A group of MPs, called "Latvia- outside NATO", plus similar groups from Russia and Ukraine, signed a declaration opposing the expansion of NATO.

- The head of the privatisation agency Janis Naglis announced the start of public offers for three large companies: Riga Carriage Plant, Riga Printing-House and Ogre Plant of knitted Goods. The offers start July 21 and last until August 15.
